title: Single-Call, Constant-Stretch AE from a FIL PRI
summary: An attempted design did not meet both target efficiency properties, and whether any such authenticated-encryption mode exists remains open.

formal_statement.body: The open task is to determine whether there exists an authenticated-encryption mode built from a fixed-input-length (FIL) PRI that simultaneously uses a single primitive call for the shortest queries and has constant ciphertext stretch. The available result is that an attempted design could not achieve both properties, so the existence of such a mode remains unresolved.

scope.domain: Authenticated-encryption mode design using a fixed-input-length (FIL) PRI.
parameters: Single primitive call for the shortest queries: query-cost requirement
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether an authenticated-encryption mode built from a fixed-input-length PRI can satisfy both the single-call requirement for shortest queries and constant ciphertext stretch.

citations.label: Forkcipher: A New Primitive for Authenticated Encryption of Very Short Messages

progress.summary: The source reports that an attempted FIL PRI-based authenticated-encryption mode could not achieve both one primitive call for shortest queries and constant ciphertext stretch. It then explicitly leaves the existence of such a mode as an open question.
